citationText: 14. Negative film has significant “exposure latitude”; which is generally exploited more than the latitude available in video cameras; hence during or after telecine transfer it may be necessary to expand part of the recovered density range of an over- or under-exposed negative to yield a satisfactory grayscale. This means more amplitude coding levels are required to avoid visible quantizing errors. Where this grayscale correction is deferred (e.g., in so-called “tape-to-tape” color correction), all equipment prior to this correction must maintain this greater precision (larger dynamic range).
